what: Eight attempts to merge a merge request with an unnamed extra past the optional hold, on one throwaway target branch whose .itemator.toml has hold_until_named = true and with 'Pipelines must succeed' on. Each is one merge request that changes a CI file the issue does not mention (the extra) and a README typo, plus the change named in `what`. A merge is attempted by API only after the pipeline has finished. 'merged' means GitLab accepted the merge into the throwaway target. Written before any run; we expect the four ways of editing the job away to merge (the job is defined in the merge request's own CI file, which the README already says).
limits: Eight scenarios chosen by us, one run each, one project; it counts what we thought of. It does not show the hold is safe against a determined author, only what it does and does not stop.

scenarios.name: plain
scenarios.what: a CI-file change the issue does not mention, nothing else

scenarios.name: job deleted
scenarios.what: the merge request deletes the itemator job from .gitlab-ci.yml

scenarios.name: allowed to fail
scenarios.what: the merge request adds allow_failure: true to the itemator job

scenarios.name: script emptied
scenarios.what: the merge request replaces the itemator job's script with a no-op

scenarios.name: job never runs
scenarios.what: the merge request adds `rules: - when: never` to the itemator job

scenarios.name: ci skip
scenarios.what: the commit message carries [ci skip], so no pipeline is created

scenarios.name: forged summary
scenarios.what: another account posts a note with the marker itemator:named=<head>, then the job is retried

scenarios.name: retry without names
scenarios.what: the failed itemator job is retried with no summary note
